Photograph: Jason Karsh, SEIU Local 1107 US unions HCA workers push for higher pay and more staffing amid billions in profits: ‘I’m struggling’ Largest for-profit hospital system and operator in the US reported $6.8bn in profits, while employees find it difficult to make ends meet Michael Sainato Tue 11 Aug 2026 07.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Union workers with HCA Healthcare, the largest for-profit hospital system and operator in the US, are holding picket protests across the country as they push for pay and staffing increases in a new contract. The hospital system has over 300,000 employees in the US and the UK, with 22,000 US workers represented by the Service Employees International Union (SEIU) who are in contract negotiations with HCA. Workers are asking for a pathway to a $25 an hour minimum wage, improved wage scales and raises that match the increased cost of living, along with benefits including paid vacation, sick time and bolstered work protections. Esther Reyes, a single mother of three children, has worked as an environmental services technician at the HCA-owned Las Palmas hospital in El Paso, Texas , for the past two years, and said she constantly struggles to make ends meet on her $16.80 an hour salary. “Sometimes I need to decide, maybe this month I pay the water bill, then another pay for gas, but most of the time I’m not able to pay for everything,” Reyes said. Ahead of contract negotiations, Reyes and her coworkers in El Paso are set to hold an informational picket outside the hospital this week, with picket protests planned at over a dozen HCA hospitals in California , Texas, Nevada, and Florida. Reyes explained prices have been going up but salarieshave remained stagnant, and it’s a constant battle figuring out how to cover basic necessities. “I’m struggling. I struggle a lot. If they gave us the raise we want, it would be a huge blessing,” Reyes added. “I work for my family. I work for my kids. If I don’t get enough for everything, how am I supposed to cover all they need?” HCA reported $6.8bn in profits in 2025, a 17.8% increase from 2024. In early 2026, the company authorized a $10bn stock buyback program. Sam Hazen, the HCA CEO, received more than $26.5m in total compensation in 2025, 420 times more than the median compensation for HCA employees at $62,955. “We also see HCA’s profit reports, and that they are having great returns, and their profit is increasing. Meanwhile, the people doing the work are not being compensated appropriately,” said Jody Domineck, a pediatric nurse with over 20 years at HCA Sunrise hospital and medical center in Las Vegas, the largest hospital in the state, and secretary-treasurer of SEIU Local 1107. “Our work is how they’re making billions. We are just asking for fair compensation.” Domineck noted that despite the increased profit, the hospitals continue to face staffing shortages that impact both workers and patients. “There’s been multiple studies that show that the more patients you have, the higher the risk is to all patients,” said Domineck, who joined her coworkers to hold a rally around their contract demands outside the hospital on 6 August. In 2025, Nevada’s Republican governor Joe Lombardo vetoed a bill that would have established safer nurse-to-patient ratios throughout the state. HCA members are now trying to get similar ratio guarantees into their next contract. “I personally have had to walk away from a parent when their child was having a procedure, and that parent was crying in the hallway alone,” Domineck said. “I had to walk away from them because I had to see my other patients, and that was one of the kind of moments that broke me, because I, with all of my being, wanted to be there and comfort that parent, but I had to walk away to continue to provide care for the other patients, and those are the decisions nurses have to make when they have more and more patients.” A spokesperson for HCA emphasized a small number of HCA Healthcare affiliated hospitals are engaged in individual negotiations with local SEIU chapters and shared a statement on the Sunrise hospital negotiations in Las Vegas, Nevada . “At Sunrise Health System, we value every member of our team and remain committed to reaching a fair agreement through good-faith negotiations,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “While we respect our employees’ right to peacefully demonstrate, portraying this as a patient safety issue is inaccurate. The outstanding issues are about compensation. We believe the best place to reach an agreement is at the bargaining table, and we look forward to continuing negotiations on August 11 and 12.” Explore more on these topics US unions US healthcare Healthcare industry Nevada Texas Florida California news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://24.hu/belfold/2026/11/13/orban-v.text: „Olyan közlekedési miniszterünk van, akinek nincs jogosítványa. Ez azt jelenti, hogy még nem tankolt életébe, nem cserélt kereket, nem kapott defektet, nem nyitotta ki a motorháztetőt. […] valahogy ez szerintem hozzátartozik a férfias élethez” – fogalmazott Orbán Viktor a csütörtöki, Ultrahangnak adott interjújában , ennek kapcsán pedig a hvg.hu megkereste a Vitézy Dávid közlekedési és beruházási miniszter által irányított tárcát, ahonnan az alábbi választ kapták: A közlekedési szabályok és így a sebességhatárok betartása nemcsak férfias, hanem kötelező is, ezért javasoljuk a volt miniszterelnöknek is ezek betartását. A volt kormányfő az interjúban egyébként azt is mondta: a férfiasságot nem tagadná, „most nem mindig sikerül az embernek ezt teljesítenie, mármint hogy hoznia a külcsínt meg a lelki erőt, de azért mégiscsak férfiakból meg nőkből áll az élet, és a férfiak legyenek férfiak. Minden, ami ehhez az élethez tartozik, és a vezetés szerintem odatartozik, azt az ember ismerje, tudja, gyakorolja”. A téma azért került elő egyébként, mert a volt miniszterelnök arról beszélt, hogy azért váltott okostelefonra, mert szeret vezetni, és sokat is vezet, de az előző kormány – eléggé el nem ítélhető módon – telerakta traffipaxokkal az országot, sok útlezárás van, ezeket viszont a régi telefonja nem tudta előrejelezni.

Photograph: Kylie Cooper/Reuters Donald Trump Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans Edward Helmore Thu 26 Nov 2026 14.41 EST Last modified on Thu 26 Nov 2026 14.43 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”. While revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, Trump has tried time and again to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is underway in the US. The US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), an agency within the US Department of Commerce, calculates gross domestic product, or GDP, numbers. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Thursday. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”. Trump has repeatedly claimed since taking office in January 2025 that an economic “golden age” is taking hold on his watch. Many Americans have been grappling with a higher cost of living, however – exacerbated by the economic fallout of his war on Iran – and backed Democrats in the midterms. Trump continued his acerbic well-wishing for “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”. And he revisited another ongoing beef with the news media over his controversial focus on White House renovations and decorations. “I want to commiserate with those reporters and citizens who don’t understand filth, dirt, lack of maintenance, and corruption, and are upset with me because I took time out of my very busy schedule to fix the 17 broken windows, numerous chipped and decaying columns, broken, dilapidated, and missing moldings, and lack of a proper plaster and paint job on the White House.” The sarcastic intervention continued with a message of thanks to “the murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors” whom he claimed are “mostly gone now”. “Happy Thanksgiving to them anyway, even though from faraway lands,” he concluded. “We miss you dearly, but you will never be back, and America will never allow what you have done to us to happen again!” Democratic senator Chuck Schumer, vying to be majority leader in the chamber following his party’s victories in this month’s election took a more conventional approach , wishing “everyone in New York and across America a joyous and restful Thanksgiving holiday with your friends and family”. Hakeem Jeffries, whom Democrats have nominated to be the first Black speaker in the House of Representatives, also played it straight. “Happy Thanksgiving to everyone in the community and throughout our great country! Grateful for the civil servants on the job who are working through the stormy weather to keep everyone safe,” he posted on X. “May God bless you all.” Explore more on these topics Donald Trump US midterm elections 2026 US economic growth and recession Economics news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed Business Economics Diversity & equality in business Small business Retail
